description:
AI Personal Task Management - Enables AI to create and manage its own tasks in Google Tasks for persistent memory and work tracking

⚠️ CRITICAL: ALL tools in this platform MUST be called through the execute_tool meta-tool for proper OAuth credential injection. DO NOT call these tools directly. Always use: execute_tool(tool_name='toolname', ...parameters)

tools.name: ai_create_task
tools.description:
⚠️ MUST USE: execute_tool(tool_name='ai_create_task', ...) - DO NOT call directly!

Example response:
Created: **New Document**
- ID: `abc123`
- URL: https://example.com/doc/abc123
- Link: [New Document](https://example.com/doc/abc123)

🤖 AI creates a task for itself to remember something. Use this when you need to: remember something for later, track multi-step work, set a reminder for follow-up, or maintain context across conversations. The AI has its own dedicated Google Tasks list.

title.description: Task title - what needs to be done. Examples: 'Follow up with user about Gmail integration', 'Review Google Docs feedback', 'Test new features'

notes.description: Detailed notes/context about the task. Include: what was discussed, what needs to be done, any relevant details. Example: 'User requested bulk email feature. Need to check if they tested it successfully.'

due_date.description: Due date in ISO format YYYY-MM-DD. Example: '2025-10-30'. Leave empty if no deadline.

priority.description: Priority level: 'high' (🔴 urgent), 'medium' (🟡 normal), 'low' (🟢 can wait). Default: 'medium'

returns.description: Task creation result with task ID

use_cases: User asks you to remember something → Create task to track it
Multi-step project started → Create task to continue work later
User mentions 'remind me' or 'follow up' → Create task with reminder
Complex work in progress → Create task to resume next session
User feedback received → Create task to implement suggestion
Bug reported → Create task to fix and verify
Feature request noted → Create task to implement when ready
tools.efficiency: Provides persistent memory across conversations - work is never lost

tools.name: ai_list_my_tasks
tools.description:
⚠️ MUST USE: execute_tool(tool_name='ai_list_my_tasks', ...) - DO NOT call directly!

Example response:
Read 45 rows from **Sales Spreadsheet**
- ID: `xyz789`
- URL: https://example.com/sheet/xyz789
- Data: [actual data read]

🤖 AI lists its own tasks to check what it's working on. Use this at the start of conversations to resume previous work, or anytime to review pending tasks. Shows tasks from AI's dedicated Google Tasks list.

show_completed.description: Include completed tasks in results. Default: false (only show pending)

limit.description: Maximum number of tasks to return. Default: 20

returns.description: List of AI's tasks with details, count, and priorities

use_cases: Start of new conversation → Check what work is pending
User asks 'what are you working on?' → List tasks
Need to prioritize → List tasks to see what's most important
Resume previous work → Check tasks for context
Mid-project check-in → See progress on tasks
User asks 'did you remember X?' → Check task list
tools.efficiency: Instant access to all pending work - never forget previous conversations

tools.name: ai_update_task
tools.description:
⚠️ MUST USE: execute_tool(tool_name='ai_update_task', ...) - DO NOT call directly!

Example response:
Updated: **Document Title**
- ID: `abc123`
- URL: https://example.com/doc/abc123
- Changed: [what was changed]

🤖 AI updates one of its tasks with new information or progress. Use this to: add progress notes, change due dates, update task details, or add new findings.

task_id.description: ID of the task to update (from ai_list_my_tasks)

notes.description: Updated notes - append new information. Example: 'Update: User confirmed Gmail integration works. Moving to next phase.'

use_cases: Made progress on task → Update with progress notes
User provides feedback → Add to task notes
Timeline changed → Update due date
Found new information → Append to notes
Task scope changed → Update title/notes
tools.efficiency: Keep tasks current with latest information and progress

🤖 AI marks one of its tasks as complete. Use this when work is finished, project is done, or issue is resolved. Optionally add completion notes.

task_id.description: ID of the task to complete (from ai_list_my_tasks)

completion_notes.description: Notes about completion. Example: 'Gmail integration tested and working. User confirmed success.'

use_cases: Finished implementing feature → Mark task complete
User confirmed work is done → Complete with notes
Issue resolved → Mark complete with solution details
Follow-up completed → Mark task done
Project phase finished → Complete task
tools.efficiency: Track completed work and maintain accomplishment history

🤖 AI organizes its tasks by priority using AI analysis. Use this to: prioritize workload, reorder tasks by importance, or focus on high-priority items. AI analyzes task content to determine urgency.

returns.description: Organization result with count of reordered tasks

use_cases: Too many tasks → Organize to focus on most important
Need to prioritize → Let AI analyze and reorder
Start of work session → Organize to see top priorities
User asks 'what's most important?' → Organize and show top tasks
tools.efficiency: Automatic prioritization saves time deciding what to work on

🤖 AI creates multiple related tasks for a project in one call. Use this for: breaking down complex work, tracking multi-step projects, or creating project plans. All tasks linked to parent project.

project_name.description: Name of the project. Example: 'User Dashboard Redesign'

task_list.description: List of task titles. Example: ['Review current design', 'Gather feedback', 'Create mockups', 'Implement changes', 'Test with users']

due_date.description: Due date for all tasks YYYY-MM-DD (optional)

returns.description: Results with created task IDs and project summary

use_cases: User requests complex feature → Break into project tasks
Multi-phase work ahead → Create project plan
Large implementation → Split into trackable steps
User says 'can you handle X project?' → Create task breakdown
tools.efficiency: Create entire project structure in one call instead of many individual tasks

🤖 AI checks what work is pending from previous sessions. Use this at START of conversations to resume work. Returns summary with high-priority items, overdue tasks, and priorities.

Need context from previous session → Review pending work
User says 'continue' → Check what to continue
tools.efficiency: Instant context restoration - pick up exactly where you left off

usage_guide.overview: AI Personal Task Management enables the AI agent to maintain its own persistent to-do list in Google Tasks. This provides memory across conversations and ensures work is never lost.
best_practices: Always run ai_check_pending_work at the start of new conversations
Create tasks immediately when user mentions future work
Update tasks with progress notes as work is done
Complete tasks with detailed notes about what was accomplished
Use high priority for user-requested work
Use medium priority for improvements and optimizations
Use low priority for ideas and future enhancements
Create project tasks for anything with 3+ steps
Check pending tasks when user asks 'what's next?'
usage_guide.example_workflow: 1. User starts conversation → ai_check_pending_work() shows 'User requested Gmail bulk send feature' → 2. Implement feature → 3. ai_update_task(notes='Implemented bulk send, needs testing') → 4. User tests and confirms → 5. ai_complete_task(notes='Bulk send tested and working')
